problem.claim: Adapt score matching and its major extensions to partially observed data, allowing any subset of coordinates to be missing.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies limited prior work on score matching when data is incomplete.

contributions.claim: Introduces two general-purpose approaches for missing-data score matching: importance weighting and a variational method.
Provides finite-sample bounds for the importance-weighting approach in finite-domain settings.

Reports that importance weighting is especially strong for small-sample, lower-dimensional cases, while the variational approach is strongest in complex high-dimensional graphical-model estimation settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work by extending score matching and its major extensions to flexible partial-missingness settings and by proposing separate importance-weighted and variational approaches.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report finite-sample bounds for the importance-weighting approach in finite-domain settings.
The authors report especially strong importance-weighting performance in small-sample, lower-dimensional cases.
The authors report demonstrating the variational approach on graphical-model estimation with both real and simulated data, where it is strongest in more complex high-dimensional settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Score matching is presented as a tool for learning data distributions across diffusion, energy-based, and graphical-model applications.
The abstract notes limited exploration of score matching with incomplete data.
The paper adapts score matching to arbitrary coordinate subsets being missing and introduces importance-weighting and variational variants.

It reports finite-sample bounds and stronger importance-weighting results in small, lower-dimensional regimes, while highlighting the variational method for complex high-dimensional graphical-model tasks on real and simulated data.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates two methods and links each to a different reported regime: importance weighting to small-sample, lower-dimensional cases and the variational approach to complex high-dimensional settings.

lessons.interpretation: A method-specific regime map can make a multi-method contribution more actionable and prevent an undifferentiated effectiveness claim.
lessons.application: When presenting several approaches, state the concrete data or task regime associated with each reported strength and place any supporting bound or demonstration beside it.
lessons.exception: Do not generalize the regime map beyond the domains, sample conditions, and tasks actually reported.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the missingness mechanism, exact assumptions, bound form, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative performance differences.
The reported high-dimensional demonstration is limited in the abstract to graphical-model estimation on real and simulated data.
